topics.topic: Identity recovery and old-to-new identity mapping for entities recreated after restore
questions: What happens to Projects, Customers, Rooms and ArtifactPointers first created after the restored backup, whose original Registry-minted identities are lost and cannot be supplied by their ordinary create or publish actions?

What fact maps each `customer_ref` minted by the lost import to the corresponding Customer and newly minted `customer_ref` after the repeated import, so consumers and recorded retention actions can relink it?

quotes: The restored store begins its own history from the backup: every change after it is lost, the audit entries with it, and Registry's guarantees — the log's numbering, the closed import — hold within each store's history.

Where the retention record or the kept export is missing, what the restored store holds stands until the owner corrects it with the ordinary owner actions from what the owner knows; a fact that cannot be reconstructed stays as the backup holds it, and the governance records that.
A repeated import mints new `customer_ref`s for the Customers it makes; a consumer that kept one the lost import minted relinks it in its own service, as R0-79 says for ids production does not hold.
Every identity Registry mints — `project_id`, `room_id`, artifact pointer id, `customer_ref` — is an opaque identifier with no meaning in its form.
Each new Customer's `customer_ref` is minted when the import is accepted.

The restored store begins its own history from the backup (R0-89): every change after the backup's instant is lost, the audit entries with it, and numbering continues from the backup's last number (A15).
judgement.divergence: One implementation records a recoverable old-to-new identity correspondence or provides a recovery path that preserves lost identities; another treats the post-backup entities as absent, mints fresh identities when they are recreated, and keeps no correspondence. The owner, consumers holding the lost identities, and governance replay keyed by those identities notice whether records can be relinked and retention actions reapplied.
judgement.why: The texts say that the identities and changes are lost and that consumers relink, but do not identify any model fact or authoritative correspondence by which the old and replacement identities are matched.

topics.topic: Scope of lifecycle transitions and project erasures recorded and replayed after restore
questions: Does the recovery record and replay obligation also cover inverse lifecycle changes—lifting a restriction and resuming a relationship—and which project erasures are included: anonymisation, deletion whole, or both?
Does the retention record and restore procedure cover the inverse Customer transitions—lifting a restriction and resuming a relationship—or only restriction and relationship-end actions?

quotes: The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before the greatest date the owner ever erased by, before configuring the tokens and starting it again.
A project the backup holds as active that was erased after it is archived first, then erased, as any project (Primary actions).
judgement.why: State 2 requires restoration to reproduce the recorded current state, including the negative Customer states, and applies the ordinary project-erasure action selected by the recorded state.

topics.topic: Which original or replayed dates lifecycle marks must retain
questions: When an erasure, restriction or other lifecycle action is repeated, does the model retain the original action date from governance or record the later replay instant as the mark's instant?

For an end-of-relationship action, does “its date” mean the action's execution date, the owner-supplied effective relationship-end date required by R0-84, or are both retained so the Customer's ended date can be reconstructed?

quotes: What the owner repeats after a restore — erasures, restrictions, ends of a relationship, the greatest date audit entries were ever erased by — follows the owner's record of the retention review (R0-60): a governance document, outside this case (Explicit exclusions), naming each action by its date, kind and the `customer_ref` or `project_id` it touched — an audit erasure by its date alone — with no personal value.
its marks, each with the instant the owner set it:
Ending a customer relationship records the date the owner gives — the day the relationship in fact ended, which may be earlier than the action — or today when the owner gives none.

The owner first starts the restored instance owner-only (A17 rule 1), so no service and no agent reaches it, and brings each Customer and project to the state the owner's own record of the retention review (R0-60) gives for it now — erased, restricted, ended or not — and erases audit entries before the greatest date the owner ever erased by, before configuring the tokens and starting it again.
judgement.divergence: One implementation writes the original governance-recorded instant into a restored lifecycle mark, while another executes the ordinary transition and records the later replay instant; for relationship ending, one treats the governance date as the effective end date while another treats it as the action date and lacks the effective date. The owner sees different mark dates, and the retention review calculates from a different relationship-end date.
judgement.why: The recovery text identifies only one action date and requires restoring the state, but it does not distinguish the original action instant, the replay instant, and the separately owner-supplied effective relationship-end date.

topics.topic: Personal-data classification of Customer fields individually versus only in combination
questions: Does this make Customer kind, the tax-id answer and the v1 `customer_ref` individually `personal_data`, contradicting State 1's classification of Customer kind and identifiers as `business_confidential`, or does only the combined bundle hold personal data because it also contains names?
